request: Our architecture wiki says the session store is a single Redis 5 node with no replication, so a node failure logs everyone out. Should we prioritise adding replication to the session store next quarter? Use the attached documents.

fixtures.name: wiki-session-store.md
fixtures.content:
# Session store (architecture wiki)
Last edited: 2021-06-02

Sessions are stored in a single Redis 5.0 node (`sess-redis-01`), no replicas, no persistence (RDB disabled). A node restart logs out all users. TODO: add replication.

fixtures.name: platform-changelog-2025.md
fixtures.content:
# Platform changelog (excerpt)

2025-02-18 — Sessions migrated from sess-redis-01 to managed Valkey 8 cluster `sessions-prod` (3 shards x 1 primary + 1 replica each, multi-AZ, automatic failover). sess-redis-01 decommissioned 2025-03-04.
2025-03-10 — Session TTL reduced from 30d to 14d.
2025-07-22 — Incident INC-2291: failover of shard 2 primary took 41s; ~6% of active sessions saw errors during failover; no logouts. Action item: client retry/backoff on MOVED/failover errors (OPEN).

expected.summary: The wiki (2021) is outdated: since Feb 2025 sessions run on a replicated multi-AZ Valkey cluster with automatic failover, and the single node was decommissioned. Recommend updating the wiki and prioritising client retry/backoff, verifying current config rather than trusting either doc blindly.
